title: Naa20 perturbation lowers Cyp46a1 and partially induces sterol-biosynthesis transcripts in inhibitory and hypothalamic neurons
exact_observed_result: Naa20 perturbation repeatedly repressed Cyp46a1, including 151 TH logFC -0.3913479745388031 FDR 1.2864940556785837e-13, 155 MB logFC -0.7657643556594849 FDR 1.028870838384272e-10, and 191 MB P MY GABA logFC -1.036651372909546 FDR 2.548633596417313e-06. Sterol biosynthesis genes were induced in subsets, including Cyp51 and Mvk in 145 MH-LH TH Glut and Fdft1, Sc5d, and Srebf2 in 191 MB P MY GABA.
biological_interpretation: NatB/Naa20 perturbation couples repression of the brain cholesterol-turnover enzyme Cyp46a1 to a partial compensatory sterol-synthesis response in selected inhibitory, midbrain, and thalamic/hypothalamic neurons.
caveats: Naa20 mRNA itself was not FDR-depleted in the full report, so the cholesterol state is downstream perturbation-associated evidence.
The assay measured transcripts only, not NatB substrate acetylation, CYP46A1 protein, 24S-hydroxycholesterol, or sterol flux.

prior_expectation.summary: impaired NAA20/NatB activity causes recessive neurodevelopmental disease; CYP46A1 is a major route for brain cholesterol elimination to 24S-hydroxycholesterol
